claims.text: Anaphylaxis: H1 blocker (eg, diphenhydramine) every 6 h until symptoms resolve.
claims.quote: Antihistamines, primarily H1 blockers (eg, diphenhydramine) but sometimes H2 blockers (eg, cimetidine), should be given every 6 hours until symptoms resolve.
Antihistamines have an onset of action of one to two hours.
claims.locator: HISTAMINE H1 AND H2 ANTAGONISTS AND CORTICOSTEROIDS

claims.text: improves erythema and pruritus but not shown to reverse upper airway obstruction or improve hypotension.
claims.quote: Although they improve cutaneous erythema and decrease pruritus, they have not been shown to reverse upper airway obstruction or improve hypotension.
claims.locator: HISTAMINE H1 AND H2 ANTAGONISTS AND CORTICOSTEROIDS

claims.text: Diphenhydramine injection (adults): 10–50 mg IV at ≤ 25 mg/min or deep IM; 100 mg if required; max 400 mg/day.
claims.quote: 10 to 50 mg intravenously at a rate generally not exceeding 25 mg/min, or deep intramuscularly; 100 mg if required; maximum daily dosage is 400 mg.

claims.text: Injection CI: nursing mothers (higher risk for infants, esp. neonates and prematures);
claims.quote: Because of the higher risk of antihistamines for infants generally, and for neonates and prematures in particular, antihistamine therapy is contraindicated in nursing mothers.

claims.text: not for use as a local anesthetic (local necrosis).
claims.quote: Because of the risk of local necrosis, this drug should not be used as a local anesthetic.
claims.locator: Contraindications: Use as a Local Anesthetic

claims.text: MAOIs prolong and intensify its anticholinergic (drying) effects.
claims.quote: MAO inhibitors prolong and intensify the anticholinergic (drying) effects of antihistamines.

claims.text: Overdose: CNS depression or stimulation (stimulation esp. in children);
claims.quote: Antihistamine overdosage reactions may vary from central nervous system depression to stimulation. Stimulation is particularly likely in pediatric patients.

claims.text: atropine-like signs (dry mouth, fixed dilated pupils, flushing, GI symptoms);
claims.quote: Atropine-like signs and symptoms, dry mouth; fixed, dilated pupils; flushing, and gastrointestinal symptoms may also occur.

claims.text: can cause hallucinations, convulsions or death.
claims.quote: overdosage may cause hallucinations, convulsions or death.
